title: Pizza With 3n Slices
summary: Given an array slices representing pizza slice sizes in a clockwise order, determine the maximum sum of slice sizes you can select by picking a slice, followed by your friend Alice picking the next anti-clockwise slice, and your friend Bob picking the next clockwise slice, continuing until all slices are picked.
statement: Given an array slices representing pizza slice sizes in a clockwise order, determine the maximum sum of slice sizes you can select by picking a slice, followed by your friend Alice picking the next anti-clockwise slice, and your friend Bob picking the next clockwise slice, continuing until all slices are picked.
constraints: slices is a positive circular array whose length is three times the number you must select.
Select exactly length/3 slices with no two selected positions adjacent around the circle.
Return the greatest possible selected sum.
hints: Break the circle into cases excluding the first slice or excluding the last slice.
For a line, DP over prefixes and exact selection counts with take or skip choices.
Taking a slice adds it to the state two positions earlier; skipping keeps the prior state.
Every legal circular selection excludes at least one endpoint, so one of the two linear cases contains the optimum.
editorial: A circular independent set cannot contain both endpoints. Solve two linear arrays, one without each endpoint. Linear DP chooses exactly n slices and uses the prefix two positions back when taking the current slice, enforcing nonadjacency. The oracle independently enumerates exact-size index subsets and checks circular neighbors.

tests.explanation: Choosing slices four and six gives ten without circular adjacency.
Choosing the second and fourth slices gives fifteen.
